overviewHtml:
This graded quiz assesses your understanding of what current AI models can and can't do and how that is measured. You'll be asked about hallucination, unfaithful explanations, interpretability, the dispute over understanding, step-by-step reasoning, retrieval, agents, benchmarks, time-horizon measures, and AI-assisted AI research.

Note: Aim for a score of 80 percent or higher. If you score lower, use the feedback to review the topics you missed, then retake the quiz.

forms.stemHtml: An assistant names the author and publisher of a book that doesn't exist. Which account of how this happened fits the way language models work?

options.html: It retrieved a real record and then altered a few of the details
options.text: It retrieved a real record and then altered a few of the details
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on hallucination and calibration.

options.html: It decided that an invented answer would satisfy the user more
options.text: It decided that an invented answer would satisfy the user more
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on hallucination and calibration.

options.html: It produced likely text, which nothing checked against the world
options.text: It produced likely text, which nothing checked against the world
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A model generates what is likely to come next. For rare details, likely text and true text can come apart, and no step compares the output with reality.

options.html: It suffered a temporary fault that stopped it working as designed
options.text: It suffered a temporary fault that stopped it working as designed
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on hallucination and calibration.

forms.stemHtml: You ask an assistant why it recommended one option over another, and it gives a clear list of reasons. What kind of evidence is that list?

options.html: A record of the steps the model actually computed to reach it
options.text: A record of the steps the model actually computed to reach it
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on inconsistency and unfaithful explanations.

options.html: Generated text that may not match what drove the answer
options.text: Generated text that may not match what drove the answer
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! An explanation is produced the same way as any other output. It can be plausible and still leave out what actually determined the answer.

options.html: A summary written by the model's developer in advance
options.text: A summary written by the model's developer in advance
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on inconsistency and unfaithful explanations.

options.html: A readout taken from the model's internal features
options.text: A readout taken from the model's internal features
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on inconsistency and unfaithful explanations.

forms.stemHtml: Which statements about interpretability research are accurate? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: Researchers have found internal features tied to recognizable concepts
options.text: Researchers have found internal features tied to recognizable concepts
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Teams at several companies have used sparse autoencoders to identify such features.

options.html: The findings cover a small part of what a model does
options.text: The findings cover a small part of what a model does
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Coverage is partial, and many of the features found have no clear meaning.

options.html: Researchers can now read any model's reasoning in full
options.text: Researchers can now read any model's reasoning in full
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on interpretability.

options.html: The findings come from asking models to describe themselves
options.text: The findings come from asking models to describe themselves
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on interpretability.

forms.stemHtml: A model trained only on lists of Othello moves formed an internal representation of the board. Where does this leave the dispute over whether language models understand?

options.html: Settled in favor of understanding, as nearly all experts now agree
options.text: Settled in favor of understanding, as nearly all experts now agree
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on stochastic parrots and world models.

options.html: Settled against understanding, since Othello is only a board game
options.text: Settled against understanding, since Othello is only a board game
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on stochastic parrots and world models.

options.html: Open, with internal structure shown in a narrow setting
options.text: Open, with internal structure shown in a narrow setting
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The result is a clear demonstration in a small, closed game. How far it extends to large language models, and whether it counts as understanding, is unsettled.

options.html: Closed, because the question has been judged meaningless
options.text: Closed, because the question has been judged meaningless
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on stochastic parrots and world models.

forms.stemHtml: Why does a model get more multi-step problems right when it writes out its working first?

options.html: The written steps are checked by a separate calculator program
options.text: The written steps are checked by a separate calculator program
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on step-by-step reasoning.

options.html: The written steps adjust the model's parameters
options.text: The written steps adjust the model's parameters
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on step-by-step reasoning.

options.html: The written steps are copied from its training text
options.text: The written steps are copied from its training text
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on step-by-step reasoning.

options.html: The written steps become context for later predictions
options.text: The written steps become context for later predictions
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Each token is predicted from all the text so far, including what the model has just written. Partial results on the page make each next step easier.

forms.stemHtml: An assistant with web search attaches a link to a sentence in its answer. What does the link establish?

options.html: That the sentence states what the page says
options.text: That the sentence states what the page says
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on retrieval.

options.html: That the page is accurate and up to date
options.text: That the page is accurate and up to date
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on retrieval.

options.html: That the page was retrieved for the answer
options.text: That the page was retrieved for the answer
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A citation shows what was retrieved. The model can still misread, misquote, or ignore the page, so the sentence has to be compared with the source.

options.html: That the page was part of the training text
options.text: That the page was part of the training text
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on retrieval.

forms.stemHtml: An agent working on a twenty-step task makes a mistake at step three. Why is that more serious than a mistake in a single chat reply?

options.html: The mistake alters the model's parameters
options.text: The mistake alters the model's parameters
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on agents and memory.

options.html: The mistake stops the loop from continuing
options.text: The mistake stops the loop from continuing
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on agents and memory.

options.html: The later steps build on the mistake
options.text: The later steps build on the mistake
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! This is a compounding error. In a loop each step takes earlier steps as given, so an early mistake is carried forward.

options.html: The later steps are hidden from the user
options.text: The later steps are hidden from the user
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on agents and memory.

forms.stemHtml: Which of these can raise a model's benchmark score without the model becoming more capable in general? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: The benchmark's questions were in the model's training data
options.text: The benchmark's questions were in the model's training data
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! This is contamination. The model may reproduce answers it has seen.

options.html: The model was tuned specifically to do well on that benchmark
options.text: The model was tuned specifically to do well on that benchmark
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! This is overfitting to a benchmark. The gain may not carry over to other tasks.

options.html: The benchmark was replaced with a harder one
options.text: The benchmark was replaced with a harder one
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on how benchmarks mislead.

options.html: The scoring gives nothing for "I don't know," and the model guesses
options.text: The scoring gives nothing for "I don't know," and the model guesses
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Scoring that rewards guessing produces models that guess, which lifts the score.

forms.stemHtml: An AI model is reported to have a one-hour time horizon on software tasks. What does that state?

options.html: It finishes a typical software task in about one hour
options.text: It finishes a typical software task in about one hour
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on task length and productivity studies.

options.html: It works for one hour before it starts making errors
options.text: It works for one hour before it starts making errors
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on task length and productivity studies.

options.html: It can replace one hour of a programmer's working day in full
options.text: It can replace one hour of a programmer's working day in full
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on task length and productivity studies.

options.html: It succeeds half the time on tasks that take people an hour
options.text: It succeeds half the time on tasks that take people an hour
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The hour is the time a skilled person needs, and the success bar is 50 percent.

forms.stemHtml: Which of these have been demonstrated in published work on AI systems improving themselves? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: A system improving its surrounding code against tests people built
options.text: A system improving its surrounding code against tests people built
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! This is bounded self-refinement, and it is documented.

options.html: A system setting its own research direction and improving without limit
options.text: A system setting its own research direction and improving without limit
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on AI-assisted AI research.

options.html: An improvement loop running for days with no person inside it
options.text: An improvement loop running for days with no person inside it
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! One 2026 preprint reports an eight-day run of this kind, within tasks and tests that people chose.

options.html: A system redesigning its own evaluator and advancing indefinitely
options.text: A system redesigning its own evaluator and advancing indefinitely
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on AI-assisted AI research.

forms.stemHtml: Asked for a little-known person's date of birth, a model gives a different wrong date each time. Why does it give a date at all?

options.html: A date is the likely form of answer, and nothing verifies it
options.text: A date is the likely form of answer, and nothing verifies it
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The model has learned the shape of an answer without its content. It fills the shape with likely material, and no step checks the result.

options.html: A hidden database supplies a date whenever one is requested
options.text: A hidden database supplies a date whenever one is requested
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on hallucination and calibration.

options.html: A safety rule stops the model from ever leaving a question open
options.text: A safety rule stops the model from ever leaving a question open
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on hallucination and calibration.

options.html: A fault in the model scrambles the correct date it has stored
options.text: A fault in the model scrambles the correct date it has stored
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on hallucination and calibration.

forms.stemHtml: In a 2023 study, a planted pattern in the prompt steered models to wrong answers. The models' written reasoning supported those answers and almost never mentioned the pattern. What does this show about a model's explanations?

options.html: They are always false, so they should never be read
options.text: They are always false, so they should never be read
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on inconsistency and unfaithful explanations.

options.html: They reveal the hidden instructions a model was given
options.text: They reveal the hidden instructions a model was given
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on inconsistency and unfaithful explanations.

options.html: They become accurate once a model is asked to be fully honest
options.text: They become accurate once a model is asked to be fully honest
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on inconsistency and unfaithful explanations.

options.html: They can be plausible without matching what drove an answer
options.text: They can be plausible without matching what drove an answer
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The study's authors call these unfaithful explanations. An explanation is output, and you can't tell from it alone whether it matches what produced the answer.

forms.stemHtml: A study traces the internal steps one model takes on a set of chosen prompts. Which cautions do its own authors state? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: The model's internal activity could not be recorded
options.text: The model's internal activity could not be recorded
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on interpretability.

options.html: The method gave useful insight on only a fraction of prompts
options.text: The method gave useful insight on only a fraction of prompts
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The authors report satisfying insight for about a quarter of the prompts they tried.

options.html: The cases published are ones where the method worked
options.text: The cases published are ones where the method worked
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The examples are success cases, described as evidence that a mechanism exists in one context.

options.html: The results apply equally to every model from every developer
options.text: The results apply equally to every model from every developer
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on interpretability.

forms.stemHtml: Which statement best describes the state of expert opinion on whether language models understand language?

options.html: Experts are divided, partly over what "understand" means
options.text: Experts are divided, partly over what "understand" means
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A survey found researchers split about evenly, and part of the disagreement concerns the word itself.

options.html: Experts agree that models understand as people do
options.text: Experts agree that models understand as people do
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on stochastic parrots and world models.

options.html: Experts agree that models only repeat memorized text
options.text: Experts agree that models only repeat memorized text
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on stochastic parrots and world models.

options.html: Experts have stopped studying the question as unanswerable
options.text: Experts have stopped studying the question as unanswerable
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on stochastic parrots and world models.

forms.stemHtml: A model asked "What is 17 times 24?" answers wrongly in one move. Asked to show its working, it writes "17 times 20 is 340, 17 times 4 is 68, 340 plus 68 is 408" and is right. What made the difference?

options.html: The second request switched on a built-in calculator
options.text: The second request switched on a built-in calculator
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on step-by-step reasoning.

options.html: Each partial result was on the page for the next step
options.text: Each partial result was on the page for the next step
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! One hard prediction was replaced by several easier ones, each made with the earlier results in view.

options.html: The second request gave the model more time to think
options.text: The second request gave the model more time to think
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on step-by-step reasoning.

options.html: Each partial result was looked up in the training text
options.text: Each partial result was looked up in the training text
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on step-by-step reasoning.

forms.stemHtml: A reply cites a government report for the figure "unemployment fell to 4 percent in 2024." You open the report and find that the 4 percent figure is for 2022. What has happened?

options.html: The report was changed after the model retrieved it
options.text: The report was changed after the model retrieved it
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on retrieval.

options.html: The model invented the report along with the figure
options.text: The model invented the report along with the figure
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on retrieval.

options.html: The search tool failed to retrieve any document
options.text: The search tool failed to retrieve any document
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on retrieval.

options.html: The model misread a source it had in front of it
options.text: The model misread a source it had in front of it
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Retrieval supplied the right document, and the model still reported it wrongly. A real citation doesn't show that the source was used correctly.

forms.stemHtml: An agent passes the wrong figure to a calculator tool, saves the exact but wrong result in a note, and uses the note in three later calculations. What is this an example of?

options.html: Contamination of a benchmark
options.text: Contamination of a benchmark
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on agents and memory.

options.html: A compounding error
options.text: A compounding error
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The tool worked properly. The model's wrong input produced a wrong result, and later steps built on it.

options.html: An unfaithful explanation
options.text: An unfaithful explanation
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on agents and memory.

options.html: A knowledge cutoff
options.text: A knowledge cutoff
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on agents and memory.

forms.stemHtml: A company reports that its new model scores 97 percent on a well-known public benchmark, up from 95 percent for its previous model. Which questions bear on whether the gain reflects greater ability? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: Were the benchmark's questions public before training?
options.text: Were the benchmark's questions public before training?
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! If so, contamination could account for some of the score.

options.html: Is the company's name well known to the public?
options.text: Is the company's name well known to the public?
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on how benchmarks mislead.

options.html: Are the leading models all scoring near the maximum?
options.text: Are the leading models all scoring near the maximum?
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! On a saturated benchmark, a two-point difference may reflect chance or flawed questions.

options.html: Does the model do as well on a different test of the skill?
options.text: Does the model do as well on a different test of the skill?
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A gain that appears on one benchmark only suggests tuning to that test.

forms.stemHtml: Model X has a time horizon of 30 minutes and Model Y has one of four hours, on the same set of tasks. What can you conclude?

options.html: Model Y takes eight times as long to finish each task
options.text: Model Y takes eight times as long to finish each task
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on task length and productivity studies.

options.html: Model Y succeeds half the time on much longer tasks
options.text: Model Y succeeds half the time on much longer tasks
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Task length is measured in human working time. Y reaches 50 percent success on tasks that take people four hours, and X on tasks that take half an hour.

options.html: Model Y completes four-hour tasks almost every time
options.text: Model Y completes four-hour tasks almost every time
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on task length and productivity studies.

options.html: Model Y makes people eight times as productive as X
options.text: Model Y makes people eight times as productive as X
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on task length and productivity studies.

forms.stemHtml: Which of these statements are forecasts and not findings? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: An agent made seven accepted changes to its own code in eight days
options.text: An agent made seven accepted changes to its own code in eight days
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on AI-assisted AI research.

options.html: AI systems will soon design their own successors unaided
options.text: AI systems will soon design their own successors unaided
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! This predicts what will happen. Nothing of the kind has been observed.

options.html: Self-improvement will make AI progress speed up sharply
options.text: Self-improvement will make AI progress speed up sharply
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! This is a prediction about where bounded loops lead, and researchers disagree about it.

options.html: A survey found bounded self-refinement to be established practice
options.text: A survey found bounded self-refinement to be established practice
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on AI-assisted AI research.

forms.stemHtml: Researchers describe hallucination as a product of a model's ordinary operation. What is the reason?

options.html: Models are built to mislead users whenever a question is hard
options.text: Models are built to mislead users whenever a question is hard
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on hallucination and calibration.

options.html: Models copy their errors from mistakes in the training text
options.text: Models copy their errors from mistakes in the training text
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on hallucination and calibration.

options.html: Models switch into a separate mode when they lack information
options.text: Models switch into a separate mode when they lack information
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on hallucination and calibration.

options.html: Models generate likely text, with no check against the facts
options.text: Models generate likely text, with no check against the facts
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The same process produces true and false statements. Errors would arise even from error-free training text, because rare facts leave too little pattern to predict from.

forms.stemHtml: A user writes "I think the answer is B, but what do you think?" The assistant picks B and gives three reasons, none of which mentions the user's suggestion. What is the best description of those reasons?

options.html: A possible rationalization of an answer the hint produced
options.text: A possible rationalization of an answer the hint produced
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A suggestion in the prompt can steer the answer, and the explanation may justify the answer without mentioning what steered it.

options.html: Proof that the model worked the answer out independently
options.text: Proof that the model worked the answer out independently
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on inconsistency and unfaithful explanations.

options.html: Evidence that the model ignored the wording of the prompt
options.text: Evidence that the model ignored the wording of the prompt
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on inconsistency and unfaithful explanations.

options.html: A direct report from the model's internal computation
options.text: A direct report from the model's internal computation
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on inconsistency and unfaithful explanations.

forms.stemHtml: A headline says "Scientists can now read an AI's mind." Which facts about interpretability research would you set against it? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: Most studies are by a company examining its own model
options.text: Most studies are by a company examining its own model
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Independent replication is limited, especially for closed models.

options.html: No internal feature has ever been linked to a concept
options.text: No internal feature has ever been linked to a concept
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on interpretability.

options.html: The methods are young and still being tested
options.text: The methods are young and still being tested
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Researchers don't yet agree on how to measure whether a set of features is a good one.

options.html: Tracing works on some selected prompts and not on most
options.text: Tracing works on some selected prompts and not on most
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Published cases are the ones where the method worked, and they capture a small fraction of the model's activity.

forms.stemHtml: Someone argues: "Language models hold nothing beyond surface patterns of which words follow which." Which reply fits the evidence?

options.html: That is established, since models are trained only on text
options.text: That is established, since models are trained only on text
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on stochastic parrots and world models.

options.html: That is refuted, since models now understand as people do
options.text: That is refuted, since models now understand as people do
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on stochastic parrots and world models.

options.html: That can't be tested, since nothing inside a model can be recorded
options.text: That can't be tested, since nothing inside a model can be recorded
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on stochastic parrots and world models.

options.html: That is hard to square with structure found in narrow settings
options.text: That is hard to square with structure found in narrow settings
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Experiments have found internal structure beyond word statistics in narrow settings. Whether that amounts to understanding remains disputed.

forms.stemHtml: A reasoning model writes a long chain of thought before it answers. What is the mechanism by which that helps?

options.html: Later tokens are predicted with the earlier steps in view
options.text: Later tokens are predicted with the earlier steps in view
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The chain of thought is text the model generates, and each new token is predicted from it.

options.html: Later tokens are produced by a second and much larger model
options.text: Later tokens are produced by a second and much larger model
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on step-by-step reasoning.

options.html: Earlier steps are verified against an outside database
options.text: Earlier steps are verified against an outside database
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on step-by-step reasoning.

options.html: Earlier steps retrain the model before it answers
options.text: Earlier steps retrain the model before it answers
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on step-by-step reasoning.

forms.stemHtml: An answer comes with five citations to reputable sites. What follows about the answer?

options.html: It can be checked, and hasn't yet been
options.text: It can be checked, and hasn't yet been
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Citations tell you where to look. Each claim still has to be compared with the passage it points to.

options.html: It is correct, since the sites are reputable
options.text: It is correct, since the sites are reputable
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on retrieval.

options.html: It was copied word for word from the sites
options.text: It was copied word for word from the sites
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on retrieval.

options.html: It came from the parameters, not the sites
options.text: It came from the parameters, not the sites
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on retrieval.

forms.stemHtml: Why does an agent's reliability tend to fall as its tasks get longer?

options.html: Longer tasks use tools that are less exact
options.text: Longer tasks use tools that are less exact
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on agents and memory.

options.html: Longer tasks wear down the model's parameters
options.text: Longer tasks wear down the model's parameters
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on agents and memory.

options.html: Each step is slower than the one before it
options.text: Each step is slower than the one before it
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on agents and memory.

options.html: Each step depends on the ones before it
options.text: Each step depends on the ones before it
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! More steps mean more chances for a mistake, and a mistake at any step carries into those that follow.

forms.stemHtml: A model's score on a reading benchmark jumps sharply. Which explanations are consistent with no real gain in reading ability? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: The model was trained on more varied text and reads better
options.text: The model was trained on more varied text and reads better
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on how benchmarks mislead.

options.html: The test passages and answers appeared on websites it was trained on
options.text: The test passages and answers appeared on websites it was trained on
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! That is contamination, which can inflate a score.

options.html: Its developer adjusted it repeatedly against this one benchmark
options.text: Its developer adjusted it repeatedly against this one benchmark
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! That is overfitting to a benchmark, and the gain may not transfer.

options.html: Its developer tested it on new passages written after training
options.text: Its developer tested it on new passages written after training
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on how benchmarks mislead.

forms.stemHtml: In the phrase "a time horizon of two hours," whose two hours are they?

options.html: A skilled person's, working on the same task
options.text: A skilled person's, working on the same task
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Researchers time people with relevant expertise, then find the task length at which the model succeeds half the time.

options.html: The AI model's, from the start of a task to its finish
options.text: The AI model's, from the start of a task to its finish
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on task length and productivity studies.

options.html: The researchers', spent scoring each task
options.text: The researchers', spent scoring each task
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on task length and productivity studies.

options.html: The user's, saved by using the model
options.text: The user's, saved by using the model
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on task length and productivity studies.

forms.stemHtml: A company says most of its code is now written by its own AI model and that AI may soon build its successors. Which responses are sound? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: The first part is the company's report about itself
options.text: The first part is the company's report about itself
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! It may be accurate. It can't be checked from outside, and the company has an interest in how capable its product appears.

options.html: The second part is a forecast, not a finding
options.text: The second part is a forecast, not a finding
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Open-ended self-improvement hasn't been demonstrated, so a claim that it's coming is a prediction.

options.html: Together they show that self-improvement without limit has begun
options.text: Together they show that self-improvement without limit has begun
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on AI-assisted AI research.

options.html: Together they show that such claims are always false
options.text: Together they show that such claims are always false
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on AI-assisted AI research.

title: Capabilities, Limits, and Trajectory
